name: Adobe Frame.io
description: Adobe Frame.io is a creative collaboration platform for organizing, reviewing, versioning, sharing, and managing media work-in-progress across accounts, workspaces, projects, folders, files, comments, and metadata.
agentUseSummary: Adobe's developer documentation names the product Frame.io and the canonical Relay provider is frame-io. This Adobe-branded queue alias mounts no second connection or tools; use the canonical Frame.io provider.

blocked.label: Connect Adobe Frame.io
blocked.description: Use the canonical Frame.io provider; no duplicate Adobe-branded connection is created.

blocked.label: Read Adobe Frame.io
blocked.description: Accounts, workspaces, projects, files, folders, versions, comments, shares, and metadata are unavailable through this alias.

blocked.label: Change Adobe Frame.io
blocked.description: Uploads, file and folder changes, comments, shares, members, permissions, webhooks, and all mutations are unavailable through this alias.

providerSetup.blocker: Adobe Frame.io and Frame.io are the same product identity. The canonical frame-io provider already owns connection and runtime state, so a second Adobe-branded slug would duplicate credentials and authority.
providerSetup.nextAction: Route Adobe Frame.io discovery to the existing canonical Frame.io provider. When its connector is upgraded, migrate that single provider from legacy API semantics to Adobe's V4 OAuth/API contract rather than creating an alias connection.

evidence.supports: Adobe's official developer surface names the product Frame.io and documents the V4 creative collaboration API for accounts, workspaces, projects, media, metadata, and workflows.
Adobe documents Frame.io V4 user and server-to-server OAuth through Adobe IMS and Developer Console, confirming a single Frame.io product identity.

Adobe documents that legacy Frame.io and V4 require migration because V4 authentication, resources, and routes are not backward-compatible; this is a canonical connector upgrade concern, not a second provider.
